topic.title: Authentication
topic.shortdesc: Configure authentication for HTTPS and SSH connections to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and other Git servers.

body.p: The Git Client supports HTTPS and SSH connections to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and more. It also includes support for ssh-agent forwarding.

p.note: For SSH connections, you can use the SSH agent to access the keys already stored in it. To enable support for SSH agent access, go to Git(Menu) Settings Preferences SSH Connections (or Git Staging View Ellipsis menu Preferences SSH Connections ) and select the Use SSH Agent option.

body.p: To access the remote repository, you need to provide your authentication details (unless you are using unprotected SSH keys). If no such information is found in the add-on's settings, you will be prompted for them.

The Git Client allows you to authenticate over HTTPS by using either a basic authentication method (username + password) or a personal access token.
GitHub no longer accepts password-based authentication.
The authentication using personal access tokens has been tested with GitHub and GitLab.
As of September 9, 2025, BitBucket app passwords can no longer be created. Use API tokens with scopes instead. An API token must be provided as the password for Basic authentication, along with the correct BitBucket username.

If you have the two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled for GitHub or GitLab, to authenticate over HTTPS, you must generate a personal access token for your profile, and back in the Git Staging view in , use the generated token value as the authentication password when asked for your credentials.

If, for example, you have been using a GitHub account but you decide to switch to another GitHub account, you would need to reset your credentials so that you will be prompted for new ones. This is because only one set of credentials for each Git platform/server is stored. To reset your credentials, go to the toolbar at the top of the Git Staging side-view, click the settings icon (a cogwheel), and select Reset all credentials.
